verdict.rationale: Elastic Observability documents its own alerting rules. They can be scoped to service, environment, or transaction level, or written as custom KQL queries, and they fire on conditions such as log aggregations crossing a threshold. When triggered, they send alerts with notifications to services or third-party incident management systems. The evidence only shows notification-type actions, not broader automated actions on events. Missing for 10: documented action types beyond notifications (e.g., webhooks, automated remediation or workflow execution), event-trigger depth beyond threshold/KQL conditions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can create a rule to send an alert when the log aggregation exceeds a threshold.
You can define rules at different levels (service, environment, transaction) or use custom KQL queries.
You can also extend your alerts with notifications via services or third-party incident management systems.
